en.title: How Hydraulics Work
en.summary: See how pressure transfers force through a hydraulic machine.
en.action: Adjust the pump and input force to see the output change.
en.why: A hands-on model makes pressure transfer easier to see.
en.limit: This is a simplified model, not an engineering design tool.

en.title: How an Electric Motor Works
en.summary: Explore how an electric motor converts electricity into motion.
en.action: Observe the motor and try switching its current on and off.
en.why: A visual model reveals parts that are usually hidden inside a motor.
en.limit: Device compatibility has not been fully tested.

en.title: Gears
en.summary: Explore how gears change direction and rotational speed.
en.action: Scroll to the fan and move its speed slider.
en.why: Interactive diagrams build an intuitive explanation of transmission.

en.title: Airfoil
en.summary: Follow the flow of air around a wing and explore flight.
en.action: Move the slider beside the opening fluid demonstration.
en.why: Animated diagrams make invisible airflow easier to explore.
en.limit: This is an educational explanation, not a professional design simulation.

en.title: CircuitJS
en.summary: Explore voltage and current on a live circuit canvas.
en.action: Observe the default circuit, then choose an example from the Circuits menu.
en.why: Schematics and simulation appear together on one canvas.
en.limit: Real circuits require attention to component ratings and safety.

en.title: Multímetro: ten functions
en.summary: Explore common measurement functions of a multimeter.
en.action: Open the lab and follow its instructions to explore the meter.
en.why: A familiar instrument offers an accessible entry to electronic measurement.
en.limit: The original page is in Spanish; follow real-world electrical safety practices.

en.title: Sonar: a robot that hears walls
en.summary: Explore how a robot uses sonar echoes to detect obstacles.
en.action: Start the lab and look for the detection-threshold control.
en.why: The lab connects sensor measurements with a mobile robot’s behavior.
en.limit: This is a simplified teaching model; not all interactions were tested.

en.title: Pendulum Lab
en.summary: Change a pendulum’s parameters and watch its motion and energy.
en.action: Pull the bob aside, release it and compare different lengths.
en.why: A familiar swinging object raises interesting questions about motion.
en.limit: Real experiments may involve additional effects.

en.title: Bending Light
en.summary: Send light through different materials and observe reflection and refraction.
en.action: Turn on the light source and adjust the angle or material.
en.why: Visible rays make it easier to compare what happens at a boundary.
en.limit: The rays are an educational representation.

en.title: Robot Arm Simulator
en.summary: Move a robot hand and watch its joints cooperate to reach a target.
en.action: Drag the hand toward the green target on the original page.
en.why: Small challenges make inverse kinematics more intuitive.
en.limit: This educational model is not a controller for a physical robot.
